newsitem.title: USA: US seeks new input on Indian land gas royalty plan.
newsitem.headline: US seeks new input on Indian land gas royalty plan.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Tuesday it was extending to April 4 the comment period on a proposal to change how it calculates royalties for natural gas produced on native American lands.

The agency extended the comment period to address industry concerns about royalties the government wanted for payments that producers received when customers bought out of high-priced contracts, MMS spokesman Mike Baugher said.
The companies say they should not have to pay royalties for natural gas that was not sold once the contracts were bought out.
MMS has scheduled a meeting on March 26 for industry, government, and native American officials to discuss the issue.
MMS is in charge of collecting royalties for oil, natural gas and minerals produced on federal and Indian lands.
Its royalty valuation proposal for Indian lands matches a plan for production on federal land, which would base most royalties on published market prices for natural gas.
